people.name: William Shakespeare
people.why: Wrote 37 plays that are still staged everywhere, and coined a startling amount of everyday English.

people.name: Isaac Newton
people.why: Gravity, the laws of motion and calculus — arguably the single most productive mind in science.

people.name: Winston Churchill
people.why: Led Britain through the Second World War, and won a Nobel Prize for literature.

people.name: Alan Turing
people.why: Broke the Enigma code and invented the theoretical basis of computing; prosecuted for being gay.

people.name: The Beatles
people.why: Four men from Liverpool who changed popular music more than anyone before or since.

events.title: Magna Carta
events.what: Barons forced the king to accept limits on his power — the seed of constitutional government.

events.title: The Industrial Revolution
events.what: Began in Britain's mills and coalfields and remade the world's economy.

events.title: The Blitz
events.what: Eight months of bombing that London still measures itself against.

events.title: The NHS and Windrush
events.what: Free healthcare at the point of use began, and the Empire Windrush brought Caribbean migrants who helped staff it.

events.title: Brexit
events.what: Britain left the European Union after a 2016 referendum, and the argument has not finished.

culture.label: Tea
culture.text: Still a genuine daily ritual, and offering one is how hospitality starts.

culture.label: The pub
culture.text: The social centre of most communities. You order at the bar, and rounds are taken in turn.

culture.label: Manner
culture.text: Understatement, apologising when someone else bumps into you, and queueing treated as a moral matter.

culture.label: Sport
culture.text: Football above all, plus cricket, rugby and a national talent for losing gracefully.

culture.label: Four nations
culture.text: England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland are distinct countries with their own institutions and identities.

talkAbout: The weather — genuinely, it is the standard opener and nobody minds.
Where they're from within the UK, which is rarely just 'Britain'.
Football, music or a good pub.
avoid: Don't call a Scot, Welsh or Northern Irish person English. Brexit and the monarchy split rooms; Northern Ireland's history needs care.

people.name: Marie Curie
people.why: The only person to win Nobel Prizes in two sciences; Polish-born, but her work was Parisian.

people.name: Charles de Gaulle
people.why: Led Free France from London and founded the Fifth Republic.

people.name: Simone de Beauvoir
people.why: The Second Sex is the founding text of modern feminism.

people.name: Claude Monet
people.why: Impression, Sunrise gave Impressionism its name and broke painting open.

people.name: Victor Hugo
people.why: Les Misérables and Notre-Dame de Paris; two million people came to his funeral.

events.title: The Revolution
events.what: The storming of the Bastille began the end of absolute monarchy and exported liberté, égalité, fraternité.

events.title: The Napoleonic Code
events.what: A civil code that still underpins the law in dozens of countries.

events.title: Laïcité
events.what: Church and state were separated by law, and French secularism still shapes fierce arguments.

events.title: The Liberation
events.what: Allied landings in Normandy and the freeing of Paris ended four years of occupation.

events.title: May 68
events.what: Student protests and a general strike of ten million shook the state and changed French society.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Meals are structured and unhurried; the gastronomic meal of the French is UNESCO-listed.

culture.label: Bonjour
culture.text: Say it on entering any shop before anything else. Skipping it is the classic tourist mistake.

culture.label: Laïcité
culture.text: Strict secularism in public institutions, defended across the political spectrum and contested at its edges.

culture.label: Sport
culture.text: The Tour de France in July, football, and rugby in the south-west.

culture.label: Debate
culture.text: Disagreeing energetically is a form of respect, not rudeness.

talkAbout: Food and wine, and the region each comes from.
Cinema and books — cultural conversation is normal, not pretentious.
Their region, which they will consider distinct from Paris.
avoid: Assuming everyone speaks English, and starting a request without bonjour. Colonial history, especially Algeria, is difficult.

people.name: Johann Sebastian Bach
people.why: The foundation almost all later Western music is built on.

people.name: Albert Einstein
people.why: Relativity rewrote space and time; he fled Germany in 1933.

people.name: Johannes Gutenberg
people.why: Movable-type printing in Europe made mass literacy, the Reformation and modern science possible.

people.name: Angela Merkel
people.why: Led Germany for sixteen years and was for much of it the most powerful politician in Europe.

people.name: Ludwig van Beethoven
people.why: Wrote the Ninth Symphony after going deaf; its Ode to Joy is the European anthem.

events.title: The Reformation
events.what: Luther's theses split Western Christianity and reshaped European politics for centuries.

events.title: Unification
events.what: Bismarck welded dozens of states into one empire, changing the balance of Europe.

events.title: Nazism and the Holocaust
events.what: The state murdered six million Jews and millions of others; confronting it is a founding duty of modern Germany.

events.title: The Wall falls
events.what: East Germans crossed freely for the first time in 28 years; reunification followed within a year.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Over 3,000 registered bread types, plus a bakery culture taken very seriously.

culture.label: Punctuality
culture.text: On time means five minutes early. Being late without warning is genuinely rude.

culture.label: Order
culture.text: Recycling is elaborate and enforced socially; so is not crossing on a red light.

culture.label: Festivals
culture.text: Oktoberfest is Bavarian, not national — Germans will point this out.

culture.label: Directness
culture.text: Frankness is meant as honesty and respect, not aggression.

talkAbout: Their region and its dialect — Germany was many states until recently.
Football, and their Bundesliga club.
Bread, beer and where to walk at the weekend.
avoid: Nazi jokes and Hitler references are not funny here and can be illegal. Oktoberfest and lederhosen are not what most Germans are like.

people.name: Leonardo da Vinci
people.why: Painted the Mona Lisa and filled notebooks with machines centuries ahead of their time.

people.name: Dante Alighieri
people.why: The Divine Comedy effectively created the Italian language.

people.name: Galileo Galilei
people.why: Pointed a telescope at the sky, confirmed Copernicus, and was tried for it.

people.name: Sophia Loren
people.why: The first performer to win an Academy Award for a non-English-language role.

people.name: Enzo Ferrari
people.why: Built the most recognisable name in motorsport out of a racing team in Modena.

events.title: The Roman Empire
events.what: Law, language, roads and cities that still structure Europe.

events.title: The Renaissance
events.what: Florence, Venice and Rome produced an outpouring of art and thought that remade Europe.

events.title: Unification
events.what: Garibaldi and Cavour turned a patchwork of kingdoms into one country.

events.title: The Republic
events.what: Italians voted out the monarchy after the fall of Fascism.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Hyper-regional and rule-bound: pasta shapes belong to specific sauces and the rules are not negotiable.

culture.label: Coffee
culture.text: Espresso standing at the bar, and cappuccino only before about eleven in the morning.

culture.label: Family
culture.text: Sunday lunch with the extended family is the fixed point of the week.

culture.label: Calcio
culture.text: Football is followed with intensity, and Serie A rivalries run through cities.

culture.label: Gesture
culture.text: Hands are part of the grammar; the gestures carry real, specific meaning.

talkAbout: Food — but ask about their region's, not 'Italian food'.
Their city and its rivalry with the next one along.
Football, art or where to eat.
avoid: Don't add cream to carbonara or pineapple to pizza in conversation. North-south prejudice and the Mafia are not light topics.

people.name: Pablo Picasso
people.why: Co-invented Cubism, and Guernica remains the twentieth century's great anti-war painting.

people.name: Miguel de Cervantes
people.why: Don Quixote is often called the first modern novel.

people.name: Antoni Gaudí
people.why: The Sagrada Família is still being built a century after his death.

people.name: Federico García Lorca
people.why: The great voice of Andalusia, murdered by Nationalists at the start of the civil war.

people.name: Rafael Nadal
people.why: Fourteen French Open titles — the most dominant record on any surface in the sport.

events.title: Al-Andalus
events.what: Nearly eight centuries of Muslim rule left the Alhambra, and a deep mark on the language and food.

events.title: A hinge year
events.what: Granada fell, Jews were expelled, and Columbus sailed — all within months.

events.title: The Civil War
events.what: A rehearsal for the Second World War that ended in Franco's dictatorship.

events.title: The transition
events.what: After Franco's death Spain built a democracy and a constitution in three years.

culture.label: Tapas
culture.text: Small plates shared standing up, moving from bar to bar rather than settling in one.

culture.label: Timing
culture.text: Lunch at two or three, dinner at ten, and the evening starts when other countries are going to bed.

culture.label: Flamenco
culture.text: From Andalusia, and a serious art with its own canon — not a floor show.

culture.label: Languages
culture.text: Catalan, Basque, Galician and Spanish are all co-official somewhere in the country.

culture.label: Fiestas
culture.text: Every town has its patron saint's week, and they are genuinely for locals.

talkAbout: Regional food and which region does it best.
Football, though be careful which club you praise.
Their town's fiesta.
avoid: Catalan and Basque independence are live and divisive. Franco and the civil war's unmarked graves are still contested.

people.name: Fernando Pessoa
people.why: Wrote under dozens of invented identities, each with its own biography and style.

people.name: Vasco da Gama
people.why: First to sail from Europe to India, opening the sea route that reshaped world trade.

people.name: Amália Rodrigues
people.why: The queen of fado; three days of national mourning followed her death.

people.name: José Saramago
people.why: The only Portuguese-language writer to win the Nobel Prize in Literature.

people.name: Cristiano Ronaldo
people.why: Five Ballons d'Or and the most-followed person on the planet.

events.title: The Age of Discovery
events.what: Portuguese ships mapped the African coast and reached India, Brazil and Japan.

events.title: The Lisbon earthquake
events.what: A quake, fire and tsunami destroyed the city and shook Enlightenment Europe's ideas about providence.

events.title: The Carnation Revolution
events.what: A near-bloodless military coup ended 48 years of dictatorship; soldiers carried carnations in their rifles.

events.title: Macau handed back
events.what: The last European colony in Asia returned to China, closing the empire.

culture.label: Fado
culture.text: Melancholy song built around saudade — a longing for something absent that has no English equivalent.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Bacalhau, said to have 365 preparations, and pastéis de nata eaten warm with cinnamon.

culture.label: Azulejos
culture.text: Blue and white tiles cover churches, stations and ordinary houses.

culture.label: Café
culture.text: A bica standing at the counter, several times a day.

culture.label: Atlantic
culture.text: Portugal faces the ocean rather than the Mediterranean, and its food and history follow.

talkAbout: Fado, and the difference between Lisbon and Coimbra styles.
Food, especially cod and pastries.
The Discoveries, and the places Portuguese is still spoken.
avoid: Don't treat Portugal as part of Spain, or speak Spanish at them by default. The colonial wars in Africa are difficult ground.

people.name: Rembrandt van Rijn
people.why: The Night Watch and a lifetime of self-portraits that track a face aging in public.

people.name: Vincent van Gogh
people.why: Sold almost nothing in his lifetime and became the most beloved painter in the world.

people.name: Anne Frank
people.why: Her diary from a hidden annexe in Amsterdam is read by schoolchildren everywhere.

people.name: Johan Cruyff
people.why: Invented Total Football as a player and then rebuilt Barcelona around the idea.

people.name: Antonie van Leeuwenhoek
people.why: A draper who ground his own lenses and became the first person to see bacteria.

events.title: The Dutch East India Company
events.what: The first company to issue tradable shares, and the origin of the modern stock market — and of a brutal colonial system.

events.title: The Golden Age
events.what: A small republic became the richest state in Europe, with the art and science to match.

events.title: The North Sea flood
events.what: 1,836 people died; the Delta Works that followed are among the great engineering projects of the century.

events.title: First same-sex marriages
events.what: The Netherlands was the first country in the world to open marriage to same-sex couples.

culture.label: Cycling
culture.text: More bikes than people, and cycling is transport rather than sport or leisure.

culture.label: Directness
culture.text: Bluntness is a courtesy here: you are being told what someone actually thinks.

culture.label: Water
culture.text: A quarter of the country is below sea level; managing water shaped its politics and its habit of consensus.

culture.label: King's Day
culture.text: On 27 April the whole country wears orange and sells its junk on the pavement.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Cheese, herring eaten from the tail, stroopwafels, and a fondness for plain food.

talkAbout: Cycling infrastructure, which they are genuinely proud of.
Water management and how the land was made.
Football, and the Cruyff tradition.
avoid: Amsterdam's coffee shops and red-light district are a tiny and tiresome part of the country. Colonial history, especially Indonesia and slavery, is being seriously reckoned with.

people.name: Socrates
people.why: Left no writing but shaped Western philosophy through his questioning; executed by the state.

people.name: Homer
people.why: The Iliad and the Odyssey stand at the head of European literature.

people.name: Maria Callas
people.why: Reinvented opera as acting as much as singing, and remains its most famous voice.

people.name: Archimedes
people.why: Worked out buoyancy, levers and an approximation of pi two millennia early.

people.name: Mikis Theodorakis
people.why: Wrote Zorba's dance and the music of Greek resistance; imprisoned by the junta.

events.title: Athenian democracy
events.what: Cleisthenes' reforms gave citizens direct rule — the origin of the word and the idea.

events.title: The fall of Constantinople
events.what: The Byzantine Empire ended, and four centuries of Ottoman rule over Greek lands began.

events.title: The War of Independence
events.what: A revolt against the Ottomans drew European volunteers, Byron among them, and created modern Greece.

events.title: The colonels
events.what: A military junta ruled for seven years, ending after the Polytechnic uprising and the Cyprus crisis.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Olive oil in everything, long shared meals, and mezedes rather than courses.

culture.label: Orthodoxy
culture.text: Name days matter more than birthdays, and Easter is the biggest event of the year.

culture.label: Philoxenia
culture.text: Literally love of strangers — hospitality is close to an obligation.

culture.label: Kafeneio
culture.text: Hours spent over one frappé is normal and is the point.

culture.label: Antiquity
culture.text: Classical ruins are everywhere and ordinary, sitting between apartment blocks.

talkAbout: Food, and which island or region does it best.
Islands — everyone has one they defend.
History, ancient and Byzantine both.
avoid: The name dispute with North Macedonia, relations with Turkey, and the Parthenon Marbles are all sensitive. The 2010s debt crisis was humiliating and is not a joke.

people.name: Leo Tolstoy
people.why: War and Peace and Anna Karenina; he later renounced his own wealth and inspired Gandhi.

people.name: Pyotr Tchaikovsky
people.why: Swan Lake, The Nutcracker and the 1812 Overture — the most performed Russian composer.

people.name: Yuri Gagarin
people.why: The first human in space, in 1961; his 108-minute flight changed what was thought possible.

people.name: Anna Akhmatova
people.why: Requiem, memorised by friends because writing it down was too dangerous, is the great poem of the Terror.

people.name: Dmitri Mendeleev
people.why: Devised the periodic table and left gaps for elements not yet discovered.

events.title: The Christianisation of Rus
events.what: Vladimir of Kyiv adopted Orthodox Christianity, shaping the culture of the region ever since.

events.title: The Revolution
events.what: Two revolutions in a year ended the monarchy and created the first communist state.

events.title: The Great Patriotic War
events.what: The Soviet Union lost around 27 million people defeating Nazi Germany; 9 May is still the biggest day of the year.

events.title: The Soviet collapse
events.what: The USSR dissolved into fifteen states, and the 1990s brought hardship most Russians remember sharply.

culture.label: Hospitality
culture.text: A guest is fed whatever the household has, insistently. Refusing food outright is awkward.

culture.label: Literature
culture.text: Poetry is memorised and quoted in ordinary conversation far more than in most countries.

culture.label: Banya
culture.text: The steam bath is a social institution — birch branches, cold plunge, and long conversation.

culture.label: Manner
culture.text: Strangers aren't smiled at; a smile is reserved for people you actually mean it towards.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Pelmeni, borscht, black bread and pickles, and long toasts at the table.

talkAbout: Literature and film, which are common ground almost anywhere.
Food, and family recipes — everyone has a dacha story.
The banya, if you get the chance to be invited.
avoid: The war in Ukraine is dangerous and divisive to discuss; many Russians abroad are exiles. Don't assume anyone's politics from their nationality.

people.name: Nicolaus Copernicus
people.why: Put the sun at the centre of the solar system and started the scientific revolution.

people.name: Marie Skłodowska-Curie
people.why: Two Nobel Prizes; she named polonium after the country that did not exist on the map at the time.

people.name: Frédéric Chopin
people.why: Wrote almost entirely for the piano, and carried Polish soil with him into exile.

people.name: John Paul II
people.why: The first non-Italian pope in 455 years, and a decisive figure in the fall of communism.

people.name: Lech Wałęsa
people.why: An electrician who led Solidarity, won the Nobel Peace Prize, and became president.

events.title: The Commonwealth
events.what: Poland and Lithuania united into one of Europe's largest states, with an elected king.

events.title: The partitions
events.what: Poland was erased from the map for 123 years, divided between three empires.

events.title: Occupation
events.what: Invaded from both sides, Poland lost about a fifth of its population, including nearly all its Jews.

events.title: Solidarity
events.what: A strike in the Gdańsk shipyard produced the Eastern bloc's first free trade union and, in time, its end.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Pierogi, bigos and żurek; a Christmas Eve supper of twelve meatless dishes with an empty place set.

culture.label: Catholicism
culture.text: Deeply woven into national identity and history, though observance among the young is falling fast.

culture.label: All Saints
culture.text: On 1 November whole cemeteries are lit with candles, and everyone travels to visit family graves.

culture.label: Vodka
culture.text: Drunk neat and cold, with food, and toasts that expect eye contact.

culture.label: Hospitality
culture.text: 'A guest in the home is God in the home' is an actual proverb, and it is meant.

talkAbout: Food, and their family's Christmas Eve traditions.
History — Poles know theirs in detail and will explain it well.
Mountains, lakes and where they go in summer.
avoid: Never say 'Polish death camps' — the camps were German, built in occupied Poland, and the phrasing causes real offence. Politics is deeply polarised.

people.name: Alfred Nobel
people.why: Invented dynamite, then left his fortune to fund the prizes that bear his name.

people.name: Carl Linnaeus
people.why: Devised the system of two-part Latin names still used for every living species.

people.name: Astrid Lindgren
people.why: Pippi Longstocking, translated into a hundred languages, and a campaigner for children's and animal rights.

people.name: Greta Thunberg
people.why: A one-person school strike in 2018 became a worldwide movement within a year.

people.name: Ingmar Bergman
people.why: The Seventh Seal and Persona made him one of cinema's most influential figures.

events.title: The Swedish Empire
events.what: Sweden was a great power controlling much of the Baltic before Russia displaced it.

events.title: Two centuries of peace
events.what: Sweden's last war ended; it has not fought one since, and stayed neutral through both world wars.

events.title: The folkhem
events.what: Social democrats built the 'people's home' — the welfare state that defines modern Sweden.

events.title: Joining NATO
events.what: Sweden abandoned two centuries of non-alignment after Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

culture.label: Fika
culture.text: A coffee-and-cake break taken seriously enough to be scheduled into the working day.

culture.label: Lagom
culture.text: 'Just the right amount' — an aesthetic and a social value against excess in either direction.

culture.label: Allemansrätten
culture.text: The right to roam: you may walk, camp and forage on almost any land.

culture.label: Midsummer
culture.text: The biggest celebration of the year — flower crowns, pickled herring and dancing round a pole.

culture.label: Consensus
culture.text: Decisions are talked through until everyone can live with them; interrupting is rude.

talkAbout: Fika, and whether they bake.
Nature and the right to roam.
Music — Sweden exports an improbable amount of it.
avoid: Don't conflate the Nordic countries; each is distinct. Immigration and integration are heated political topics.

people.name: Roald Amundsen
people.why: First to the South Pole, first through the Northwest Passage; vanished on a rescue flight.

people.name: Henrik Ibsen
people.why: A Doll's House and Hedda Gabler invented modern realist drama.

people.name: Edvard Munch
people.why: The Scream is one of the few paintings everyone on earth recognises.

people.name: Fridtjof Nansen
people.why: Crossed Greenland on skis, then won the Nobel Peace Prize for refugee work.

people.name: Edvard Grieg
people.why: The Peer Gynt suites made Norwegian folk melody part of the world's concert repertoire.

events.title: The Viking Age
events.what: Norse seafarers raided, traded and settled from Newfoundland to Baghdad.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Norway dissolved its union with Sweden peacefully and chose a king by referendum.

events.title: Occupation and resistance
events.what: German occupation, and the heavy-water sabotage at Vemork that set back the Nazi nuclear programme.

events.title: Oil in the North Sea
events.what: The Ekofisk find funded a sovereign wealth fund now worth over a trillion dollars.

culture.label: Friluftsliv
culture.text: Open-air life. Norwegians say they are born with skis on, and the cabin weekend is close to compulsory.

culture.label: 17 May
culture.text: Constitution Day: children's parades, national dress and no military display at all.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Salmon, cod and brown cheese; the coastal cuisine is built on preservation.

culture.label: Manner
culture.text: Reserved with strangers, warm once known; small talk is not a habit.

culture.label: Landscape
culture.text: Fjords, midnight sun in summer and polar night in winter above the Arctic Circle.

talkAbout: Skiing, hiking and their cabin.
17 May and how families celebrate it.
The fjords, and which part of the coast they come from.
avoid: Whaling and the oil fund draw criticism abroad that Norwegians find simplistic. Don't lump Norway in with Sweden.

people.name: Henri Dunant
people.why: Founded the Red Cross after witnessing the aftermath of Solferino; first Nobel Peace Prize.

people.name: Carl Jung
people.why: Introversion, archetypes and the collective unconscious all come from his work.

people.name: Roger Federer
people.why: Twenty Grand Slam titles and a style that made him the sport's most admired player.

people.name: Le Corbusier
people.why: Swiss-born, and the most influential and most argued-about architect of the twentieth century.

people.name: Jean-Jacques Rousseau
people.why: The Social Contract shaped the French Revolution and modern democratic theory.

events.title: The founding pact
events.what: Three cantons swore an alliance; Swiss National Day on 1 August marks it.

events.title: Marignano
events.what: A crushing defeat that turned Switzerland towards the neutrality it has kept ever since.

events.title: The Red Cross
events.what: Founded in Geneva, and the origin of the Geneva Conventions.

events.title: Women get the vote
events.what: Federal suffrage came remarkably late; one canton held out until a court order in 1990.

culture.label: Direct democracy
culture.text: Referendums four times a year on everything from pensions to cow horns.

culture.label: Four languages
culture.text: German, French, Italian and Romansh, with real cultural differences between the regions.

culture.label: Punctuality
culture.text: The trains genuinely run to the minute, and lateness is a small moral failing.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Fondue and raclette in winter, rösti, and chocolate taken very seriously.

culture.label: Mountains
culture.text: Hiking and skiing are national habits, not tourist activities.

talkAbout: Hiking, skiing and which canton they're from.
Direct democracy and what is being voted on next.
Cheese and chocolate, both with strong regional loyalties.
avoid: Banking secrecy and the country's wartime record are sensitive. Don't assume all Swiss speak German.

people.name: James Joyce
people.why: Ulysses reinvented the novel; Bloomsday on 16 June is celebrated in the streets of Dublin.

people.name: Michael Collins
people.why: Led the IRA in the War of Independence, negotiated the Treaty, and was killed in the civil war it caused.

people.name: Mary Robinson
people.why: Ireland's first woman president, then UN High Commissioner for Human Rights.

people.name: Seamus Heaney
people.why: Nobel laureate who found the whole of Ireland in a farm in County Derry.

people.name: Oscar Wilde
people.why: The wittiest man of his age, imprisoned for being gay and dead at 46.

events.title: The Great Famine
events.what: A million died and a million emigrated; the population has still not returned to its 1841 level.

events.title: The Easter Rising
events.what: A failed rebellion whose executions turned public opinion towards independence.

events.title: Independence and partition
events.what: The Free State was created and the island divided, immediately followed by civil war.

events.title: The Good Friday Agreement
events.what: Ended thirty years of conflict in Northern Ireland.

culture.label: Music
culture.text: Traditional sessions in pubs are informal and unpaid — musicians simply turn up and play.

culture.label: The craic
culture.text: Good conversation and company, valued above almost anything; slagging is affectionate.

culture.label: Gaeilge
culture.text: Irish is the first official language, taught in every school and spoken daily in the Gaeltacht.

culture.label: GAA
culture.text: Hurling and Gaelic football are amateur, county-based, and enormous.

culture.label: Tea
culture.text: Made strong, offered constantly, and refused only with difficulty.

talkAbout: Music, and whether they play.
Their county, and the GAA.
Writers — Ireland has an unreasonable number for its size.
avoid: Don't call Ireland part of Britain. The Troubles and the border need care, and 'Paddy' and leprechaun jokes wear thin fast.

people.name: Björk
people.why: One of the most original artists of the last forty years, and Iceland's best-known face.

people.name: Snorri Sturluson
people.why: Wrote down the Norse myths; nearly everything known about them comes through him.

people.name: Halldór Laxness
people.why: Nobel laureate in 1955; Independent People is the great Icelandic novel.

people.name: Vigdís Finnbogadóttir
people.why: The world's first democratically elected woman head of state, in 1980.

people.name: Leif Erikson
people.why: Reached North America around 1000, five centuries before Columbus.

events.title: The Alþingi founded
events.what: At Þingvellir, the oldest surviving parliament in the world began meeting.

events.title: The Laki eruption
events.what: An eight-month eruption killed a fifth of Icelanders and caused famine as far away as Europe.

events.title: The Republic
events.what: Iceland declared independence from Denmark while Denmark was under German occupation.

events.title: The banking collapse
events.what: All three major banks failed within days; the Pots and Pans revolution and prosecutions followed.

culture.label: Books
culture.text: Jólabókaflóð — the Christmas book flood — means books are given on Christmas Eve and read that night.

culture.label: Pools
culture.text: Every town has a geothermal pool, and the hot tub is where the community actually talks.

culture.label: Names
culture.text: Patronymics, not surnames: Jón's daughter is Jónsdóttir. The phone book is alphabetised by first name.

culture.label: Volcanoes
culture.text: Sitting on the mid-Atlantic ridge, Iceland erupts regularly and heats itself with the results.

culture.label: Folklore
culture.text: Roads have occasionally been rerouted around rocks said to be elf dwellings — sincerity levels vary.

talkAbout: The pools, and the etiquette of showering before you get in.
Books and the Christmas book flood.
Volcanoes and the last eruption.
avoid: Elf questions are a tired joke. Whaling divides Icelanders and is not a good opener.

people.name: Jean Sibelius
people.why: Finlandia became a rallying point for independence under Russian rule.

people.name: Tove Jansson
people.why: Created the Moomins, and wrote sharp adult fiction alongside them.

people.name: Alvar Aalto
people.why: Shaped modernism with wood and curves, and designed the furniture to go inside.

people.name: Carl Gustaf Mannerheim
people.why: Commanded Finland's defence in the Winter War and became president.

people.name: Linus Torvalds
people.why: Wrote the Linux kernel and Git; both now run much of the world's computing.

events.title: The Kalevala
events.what: Elias Lönnrot's compiled folk epic gave Finland a national literature and identity.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Finland broke from Russia during the revolution, then fought a bitter civil war.

events.title: The Winter War
events.what: Finland held off a Soviet invasion for 105 days against overwhelming odds.

events.title: Joining NATO
events.what: Ended decades of non-alignment, doubling NATO's border with Russia.

culture.label: Sauna
culture.text: Over three million saunas for 5.5 million people. Business and family life both happen in them.

culture.label: Sisu
culture.text: Stubborn endurance in the face of difficulty — the closest thing to a national creed.

culture.label: Silence
culture.text: Comfortable silence is normal; filling it with chatter is what seems odd.

culture.label: Coffee
culture.text: The highest consumption per head in the world, by a clear margin.

culture.label: Nature
culture.text: 188,000 lakes, everyman's right to roam, and long summer nights that never go dark.

talkAbout: Sauna, and the correct way to do it.
Nature, berry picking and the summer cottage.
Ice hockey, especially against Sweden.
avoid: Finland is Nordic but not Scandinavian, and Finnish is not related to Swedish — both are worth getting right. Don't push for constant conversation.

people.name: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart
people.why: Over 600 works before dying at 35; arguably the most naturally gifted musician who ever lived.

people.name: Sigmund Freud
people.why: Invented psychoanalysis in Vienna and changed how the West thinks about the mind.

people.name: Gustav Klimt
people.why: The Kiss is among the most reproduced paintings in the world.

people.name: Maria Theresa
people.why: Ruled the Habsburg lands for forty years, introduced compulsory schooling, and had sixteen children.

people.name: Bertha von Suttner
people.why: Lay Down Your Arms persuaded Nobel to create a peace prize, which she then won.

events.title: The siege of Vienna
events.what: The Ottoman advance into Europe was turned back at the city walls.

events.title: Austria-Hungary
events.what: A multinational empire of a dozen peoples that dissolved at the end of the First World War.

events.title: The Anschluss
events.what: Nazi Germany annexed Austria; the country's role as perpetrator as well as victim took decades to admit.

events.title: The State Treaty
events.what: Austria regained full sovereignty and declared permanent neutrality.

culture.label: Kaffeehaus
culture.text: Vienna's coffee houses are UNESCO-listed; one coffee buys you a table for the afternoon.

culture.label: Music
culture.text: Mozart, Haydn, Schubert, Mahler and Strauss all worked here; the New Year concert is broadcast worldwide.

culture.label: Skiing
culture.text: Alpine skiing is close to a national sport and Austrian racers dominate it.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Schnitzel, Tafelspitz and Sachertorte, with an entire vocabulary for cake.

culture.label: Formality
culture.text: Titles are used in address, and greetings are more formal than in Germany.

talkAbout: Coffee houses, and which one they favour.
Music and opera.
Skiing and mountain huts.
avoid: Don't treat Austria as part of Germany. The Anschluss and Austria's Nazi past are sensitive, and Sound of Music references are met with blank looks.

people.name: René Magritte
people.why: 'This is not a pipe' and the bowler-hatted men made surrealism into everyday visual language.

people.name: Hergé
people.why: Created Tintin and, with him, the European comic album as an art form.

people.name: Adolphe Sax
people.why: Invented the saxophone, without which jazz would sound entirely different.

people.name: Eddy Merckx
people.why: Five Tours de France and 525 career wins; nicknamed The Cannibal for good reason.

people.name: Georges Lemaître
people.why: Proposed the expanding universe and what became the Big Bang theory.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Belgium broke from the Netherlands after a revolt that started at the opera.

events.title: The Congo Free State
events.what: Leopold II ran the Congo as private property; millions died, and Belgium is still reckoning with it.

events.title: The invasion
events.what: Germany's march through neutral Belgium brought Britain into the First World War; Flanders became its graveyard.

events.title: Brussels becomes Europe's capital
events.what: The EEC set up in Brussels, and the city became the administrative centre of the European project.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Chips were invented here and are served from a friterie with mayonnaise; also waffles, chocolate and mussels.

culture.label: Beer
culture.text: Belgian beer culture is UNESCO-listed — Trappist ales, lambics and a specific glass for every one.

culture.label: Two communities
culture.text: Dutch-speaking Flanders and French-speaking Wallonia, with separate media, parties and schools.

culture.label: Comics
culture.text: Comics are a mainstream adult medium here, with murals across Brussels.

culture.label: Manner
culture.text: Self-deprecating and surreal humour, and a deep suspicion of anyone taking themselves too seriously.

talkAbout: Beer and food, both endlessly.
Comics, and which series they grew up on.
Cycling, especially the spring classics.
avoid: The Flemish–Walloon divide is genuinely delicate; guessing wrong about someone's language is awkward. Congo colonial history is serious ground.

people.name: Taras Shevchenko
people.why: Born a serf, he made Ukrainian a literary language and is the country's national symbol.

people.name: Lesya Ukrainka
people.why: Wrote major drama in Ukrainian while chronically ill, and shaped the modern literature.

people.name: Serhiy Zhadan
people.why: The leading voice of the Donbas in fiction and poetry, and a wartime volunteer.

people.name: Volodymyr Zelenskyy
people.why: A comedian who played a president on television, then became one, and stayed in Kyiv in 2022.

people.name: Kazimir Malevich
people.why: Born in Kyiv; Black Square pushed abstraction as far as it could go.

events.title: Kyivan Rus
events.what: A powerful medieval state centred on Kyiv, claimed as ancestor by several modern countries.

events.title: The Holodomor
events.what: A Soviet-engineered famine killed millions; many countries now recognise it as genocide.

events.title: Chernobyl
events.what: The world's worst nuclear accident, and a major blow to Soviet credibility.

events.title: The Maidan revolution
events.what: Mass protests removed a president; Russia then annexed Crimea and war began in the Donbas.

events.title: The full-scale invasion
events.what: Russia invaded on 24 February; Ukraine's defence of Kyiv reshaped European security.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Borscht — Ukrainian borscht is UNESCO-listed — plus varenyky and salo.

culture.label: Pysanky
culture.text: Wax-resist decorated eggs, with regional patterns going back to pre-Christian symbolism.

culture.label: Vyshyvanka
culture.text: The embroidered shirt is worn with pride and has its own national day in May.

culture.label: Sunflowers
culture.text: The national flower, and a wartime symbol; Ukraine is among the world's largest producers.

culture.label: Music
culture.text: From polyphonic village singing to Kalush Orchestra winning Eurovision in 2022.

talkAbout: Food, especially borscht and who makes it best.
Music and literature — there is a great deal outsiders don't know.
Their home city, and what it was like before.
avoid: Don't call it 'the Ukraine', don't treat Ukrainian culture as a branch of Russian, and don't ask people to relive what they've been through.

people.name: Franz Kafka
people.why: The Trial and Metamorphosis gave a word to bureaucratic nightmare; he wrote in German, in Prague.

people.name: Václav Havel
people.why: Dissident, imprisoned, then president of a free country within months.

people.name: Antonín Dvořák
people.why: The New World Symphony, written in America but soaked in Bohemian melody.

people.name: Alphonse Mucha
people.why: Defined Art Nouveau posters, then spent twenty years on the Slav Epic.

people.name: Milada Horáková
people.why: Survived the Nazis and was executed by the communists in a show trial; a symbol of resistance to both.

events.title: Jan Hus burned
events.what: A church reformer executed a century before Luther, sparking the Hussite wars.

events.title: The Defenestration of Prague
events.what: Officials thrown from a castle window began the Thirty Years' War.

events.title: The Prague Spring
events.what: Reforms toward 'socialism with a human face' were crushed by Warsaw Pact tanks.

events.title: The Velvet Revolution
events.what: Communism ended in six weeks without bloodshed; the country split peacefully in 1993.

culture.label: Beer
culture.text: The highest consumption per head in the world, and Pilsner was invented in Plzeň in 1842.

culture.label: Hiking
culture.text: A national network of colour-marked trails, walked by families every weekend.

culture.label: Humour
culture.text: Dry, absurd and sceptical of authority — the Good Soldier Švejk is the national character.

culture.label: Puppets
culture.text: Marionette theatre kept the Czech language alive under Habsburg rule and is still performed.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Svíčková, goulash and knedlíky — bread dumplings that come with almost everything.

talkAbout: Beer, and which brewery they prefer.
Hiking and weekend cottages.
1989 and how quickly everything changed.
avoid: It's Czechia or the Czech Republic, not Czechoslovakia — that ended in 1993. Don't assume Prague is the whole country.

people.name: Franz Liszt
people.why: Invented the modern piano recital and was the first true musical celebrity.

people.name: Ernő Rubik
people.why: Made the Cube as a teaching aid; it became the best-selling puzzle ever.

people.name: John von Neumann
people.why: Game theory, quantum mechanics and the architecture behind nearly every computer.

people.name: Béla Bartók
people.why: Recorded peasant music across the Balkans and built a modernist language from it.

people.name: Ignaz Semmelweis
people.why: Worked out that doctors should wash their hands; was ridiculed and died in an asylum.

events.title: The Magyar conquest
events.what: Seven tribes settled the Carpathian Basin, bringing a language unrelated to any neighbour's.

events.title: The revolution
events.what: A revolt against Habsburg rule, defeated with Russian help; 15 March is still a national day.

events.title: Trianon
events.what: Hungary lost two-thirds of its territory and a third of its Hungarian speakers; the grievance persists.

events.title: The uprising
events.what: Hungarians rose against Soviet rule and were crushed in twelve days; 200,000 fled.

culture.label: Paprika
culture.text: In everything from goulash to fish soup, sweet or hot, and grown around Szeged and Kalocsa.

culture.label: Thermal baths
culture.text: Budapest sits on hot springs; Széchenyi and Gellért are civic institutions with chess boards in the water.

culture.label: Language
culture.text: Hungarian is Uralic — related to Finnish and Estonian, and to nothing else nearby.

culture.label: Wine
culture.text: Tokaji was the first classified wine region in the world, in 1737.

culture.label: Toasting
culture.text: Traditionally no clinking of beer glasses, a habit dating from 1849.

talkAbout: Thermal baths and which one to go to.
Food, especially the arguments over goulash.
The language, and how nothing else sounds like it.
avoid: Trianon and the Hungarian minorities in neighbouring states are emotive. Domestic politics is bitterly polarised.

people.name: Hans Christian Andersen
people.why: The Little Mermaid and The Ugly Duckling are told in nearly every language on earth.

people.name: Niels Bohr
people.why: Worked out the structure of the atom and led the Copenhagen school of quantum mechanics.

people.name: Søren Kierkegaard
people.why: The father of existentialism, writing from a small city under a stack of pseudonyms.

people.name: Karen Blixen
people.why: Out of Africa and Babette's Feast, written in English and Danish both.

people.name: Ole Kirk Christiansen
people.why: A carpenter who founded LEGO; the interlocking brick came from his workshop in Billund.

events.title: Harald Bluetooth converts
events.what: The Jelling stones record Denmark's Christianisation; Bluetooth technology is named after him.

events.title: The constitution
events.what: Denmark moved from absolute monarchy to constitutional rule without a revolution.

events.title: The rescue of the Danish Jews
events.what: Some 7,000 people were ferried to Sweden in fishing boats, ahead of the planned round-up.

events.title: First registered partnerships
events.what: Denmark became the first country in the world to legally recognise same-sex couples.

culture.label: Hygge
culture.text: Candles, close company and low light through a long winter. It is a real practice, not a marketing idea.

culture.label: Cycling
culture.text: More bikes than cars in Copenhagen, and cycling in ordinary clothes at all ages.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Smørrebrød open sandwiches with a strict order of eating, and the New Nordic movement that came out of Noma.

culture.label: Jantelov
culture.text: An unwritten rule against thinking yourself better than others; it shapes how people talk about success.

culture.label: Sociability
culture.text: Reserved with strangers, very warm within a group, and drinks do much of the work.

talkAbout: Cycling and city design.
Food, and the Nordic restaurant scene.
Hygge — though ask what it actually means to them.
avoid: Don't call a Dane Swedish. Immigration policy is contentious, and Greenland's relationship with Denmark is a serious subject.

people.name: Nikola Tesla
people.why: Alternating current and the induction motor; born in Croatia to a Serb family.

people.name: Marco Polo
people.why: Croatia and Venice both claim him; Korčula insists he was born there.

people.name: Luka Modrić
people.why: Won the Ballon d'Or in 2018 and took Croatia to a World Cup final.

people.name: Ivan Meštrović
people.why: The first living artist to be given a solo show at the Metropolitan Museum in New York.

people.name: Slavenka Drakulić
people.why: Her essays on life under and after communism are read across Europe.

events.title: The Republic of Ragusa
events.what: Dubrovnik was an independent maritime republic that abolished slavery in 1416.

events.title: Into Yugoslavia
events.what: Croatia joined the new South Slav kingdom after the Habsburg empire dissolved.

events.title: The war of independence
events.what: Croatia broke from Yugoslavia; Vukovar was destroyed and Dubrovnik shelled.

events.title: Joining the EU
events.what: Croatia became the 28th member, and adopted the euro a decade later.

culture.label: Coast
culture.text: Over a thousand islands along the Adriatic, and the coast is the summer centre of national life.

culture.label: The necktie
culture.text: The cravat comes from Croatian mercenaries in seventeenth-century France — hence 'cravate'.

culture.label: Klapa
culture.text: Unaccompanied male harmony singing from Dalmatia, UNESCO-listed.

culture.label: Sport
culture.text: A country of under four million reaching a World Cup final, plus water polo and handball.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Adriatic seafood and olive oil on the coast, paprika and meat inland — two different cuisines.

talkAbout: The islands and the coast.
Football, and the 2018 World Cup.
Food, and the difference between coastal and continental cooking.
avoid: The 1990s wars, and Croatia's Second World War Ustaše past, are both raw. Don't lump Croatia in with 'the Balkans' casually.

people.name: Nikola Tesla
people.why: Ethnic Serb whose alternating-current system powers the world; Belgrade's airport and museum carry his name.

people.name: Novak Djokovic
people.why: The most Grand Slam singles titles in the history of men's tennis.

people.name: Ivo Andrić
people.why: The Bridge on the Drina won the Nobel Prize and explains the region better than most histories.

people.name: Mihajlo Pupin
people.why: His inductance coils made long-distance telephony possible.

people.name: Marina Abramović
people.why: The most famous performance artist alive, and the person who defined the form.

events.title: The Battle of Kosovo
events.what: A defeat by the Ottomans that became the central story of Serbian national identity.

events.title: Sarajevo
events.what: The assassination of Franz Ferdinand by a Bosnian Serb triggered the First World War.

events.title: The Yugoslav wars
events.what: Yugoslavia broke apart in a decade of wars, ending with NATO's bombing of Serbia over Kosovo.

events.title: The Bulldozer Revolution
events.what: Mass protests removed Slobodan Milošević after he refused to accept an election result.

culture.label: Rakija
culture.text: Homemade fruit brandy, offered on arrival, and every family thinks theirs is best.

culture.label: Kafana
culture.text: Part tavern, part living room — hours of talk, food and live music.

culture.label: Brass
culture.text: The Guča trumpet festival draws hundreds of thousands for several days of relentless brass.

culture.label: Slava
culture.text: Each family celebrates its own patron saint's day, and the house is open to anyone who calls.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Ćevapi, pljeskavica and ajvar, with portions sized for farm work.

talkAbout: Food and rakija, and their family's slava.
Sport — tennis, basketball and water polo are all national strengths.
Music, from brass bands to the Belgrade club scene.
avoid: Kosovo, the 1990s wars and the NATO bombing are all deeply contested. Don't assume a shared narrative with their neighbours.

people.name: France Prešeren
people.why: The national poet; a verse of his Zdravljica is the national anthem.

people.name: Jože Plečnik
people.why: Redesigned Ljubljana almost single-handedly; his work there is World Heritage-listed.

people.name: Luka Dončić
people.why: One of the NBA's biggest stars, from a country of two million.

people.name: Primož Trubar
people.why: Printed the first books in Slovene and effectively founded the written language.

people.name: Slavoj Žižek
people.why: The most widely read living philosopher, and among the most argued about.

events.title: The first Slovene books
events.what: Trubar's catechism and primer began Slovene as a written language.

events.title: Into Yugoslavia
events.what: Slovene lands left Austria-Hungary and joined the new South Slav state.

events.title: The Ten-Day War
events.what: Slovenia's independence war lasted ten days with under a hundred deaths — by far the shortest of the Yugoslav wars.

events.title: Joining the EU and NATO
events.what: Slovenia joined both, and adopted the euro three years later.

culture.label: Beekeeping
culture.text: A national passion with painted hive panels; Slovenia proposed World Bee Day and got it.

culture.label: Outdoors
culture.text: Over half the country is forest, and Triglav's summit is treated as a rite of passage.

culture.label: Sport
culture.text: Basketball, ski jumping and cycling all well beyond what the population would suggest.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Potica, a rolled nut cake, and štruklji; Alpine, Mediterranean and Pannonian cooking in one small country.

culture.label: Language
culture.text: Slovene keeps the dual number — a separate grammatical form for exactly two.

talkAbout: Mountains, hiking and Lake Bled.
Beekeeping and honey.
Basketball, and Dončić.
avoid: Slovenia is not Slovakia, and mixing them up is a standing irritation. Don't lump it in with the Balkans — Slovenes look to central Europe.

people.name: Mother Teresa
people.why: Ethnic Albanian, Nobel Peace Prize winner, and the country's most famous name abroad.

people.name: Skanderbeg
people.why: Held off the Ottoman Empire for 25 years; the national hero and the flag's eagle.

people.name: Ismail Kadare
people.why: Wrote allegorical novels under a dictatorship and became Albania's international literary voice.

people.name: Dua Lipa
people.why: Kosovo-Albanian, and one of the biggest pop stars in the world.

people.name: Inva Mula
people.why: Sang the Diva Dance in The Fifth Element and performs at the world's major opera houses.

events.title: Skanderbeg's revolt
events.what: A quarter-century of resistance that delayed Ottoman expansion into Italy.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Albania declared independence from the Ottoman Empire at Vlorë.

events.title: Hoxha's Albania
events.what: One of the most isolated regimes on earth, which banned religion and built 170,000 concrete bunkers.

events.title: The pyramid scheme collapse
events.what: Investment schemes holding much of the country's savings failed, and the state briefly collapsed.

culture.label: Besa
culture.text: A code of honour requiring you to keep your word and protect a guest — Albanians sheltered Jews on this basis in the 1940s.

culture.label: Coffee
culture.text: Albania has more cafés per head than anywhere in Europe, and they are where everything happens.

culture.label: Bunkers
culture.text: Concrete bunkers still dot the countryside; some are now bars and museums.

culture.label: Iso-polyphony
culture.text: Southern Albanian multi-part singing, UNESCO-listed, unlike anything else in Europe.

culture.label: Gestures
culture.text: A head shake can mean yes and a nod no — worth knowing before you agree to something.

talkAbout: Besa and traditional hospitality.
The coast and mountains, which few visitors expect.
Coffee culture.
avoid: Organised crime clichés are resented. Kosovo, and relations with Serbia and Greece, need care.

people.name: Saints Cyril and Methodius
people.why: Created the first Slavic alphabet; their disciples worked at Ohrid, which became a centre of Slavic literacy.

people.name: Goce Delčev
people.why: Led the movement against Ottoman rule; claimed as a national hero by both North Macedonia and Bulgaria.

people.name: Kiro Gligorov
people.why: Steered the country out of Yugoslavia without a war.

people.name: Toše Proeski
people.why: The Balkans' biggest pop star of his generation; his death at 26 brought a national day of mourning.

people.name: Blaže Koneski
people.why: Codified the modern Macedonian literary language.

events.title: The Ilinden uprising
events.what: A revolt against the Ottomans that briefly declared a republic at Kruševo; 2 August is the national day.

events.title: The Skopje earthquake
events.what: Destroyed 80% of the capital; the world sent help and the city was rebuilt in modernist style.

events.title: Independence
events.what: The only Yugoslav republic to leave without fighting.

events.title: The Prespa Agreement
events.what: The country renamed itself North Macedonia, settling a 27-year dispute with Greece and opening NATO membership.

culture.label: Ohrid
culture.text: One of Europe's oldest and deepest lakes, with 365 churches said to line its shore.

culture.label: Music
culture.text: Complex asymmetric rhythms — 7/8 and 11/8 are ordinary dance meters here.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Ajvar made in bulk each autumn, tavče gravče beans, and shopska salad.

culture.label: Sociability
culture.text: Long coffees and unhurried conversation; nobody is in a hurry to leave a table.

culture.label: Mix
culture.text: Orthodox and Muslim communities, Macedonian and Albanian, in one small country.

talkAbout: Lake Ohrid and the churches.
Food, especially ajvar season.
Music and dance rhythms.
avoid: The name dispute with Greece and identity questions with Bulgaria are exhausting and delicate. Ethnic Macedonian–Albanian relations need care.

people.name: Constantin Brâncuși
people.why: Stripped sculpture back to essential form and became one of modernism's founders.

people.name: Nadia Comăneci
people.why: The first perfect 10 in Olympic gymnastics, at fourteen, in Montreal.

people.name: Vlad the Impaler
people.why: A ruthless defender against the Ottomans, and the loose inspiration for Dracula.

people.name: Eugène Ionesco
people.why: Rhinoceros and The Bald Soprano founded the theatre of the absurd.

people.name: George Enescu
people.why: Romania's greatest musician; the national festival and concert hall carry his name.

events.title: Roman Dacia
events.what: Rome's occupation left a Latin language surrounded by Slavic and Hungarian neighbours.

events.title: Unification
events.what: The principalities united and Greater Romania was completed after the First World War.

events.title: Ceaușescu
events.what: A personality cult, crushing austerity to repay foreign debt, and demolition of much of old Bucharest.

events.title: The revolution
events.what: The only violent overthrow of communism in Europe; over a thousand died and Ceaușescu was executed.

culture.label: Language
culture.text: A Romance language, closer to Italian than to any neighbour, which surprises most visitors.

culture.label: Painted monasteries
culture.text: The Bucovina monasteries have their entire exteriors frescoed, and are World Heritage-listed.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Sarmale, mămăligă and mici, with țuică plum brandy before the meal.

culture.label: Carpathians
culture.text: Europe's largest populations of brown bears, wolves and lynx, and vast old-growth forest.

culture.label: Music
culture.text: Doina laments and fast lăutari fiddle bands, plus the panpipe tradition.

talkAbout: The Carpathians, wildlife and hiking.
Food, and homemade țuică.
The language, and its Latin roots.
avoid: Dracula gets old quickly. Don't confuse Romanians with Roma — the conflation is common abroad and resented, and Roma face real discrimination.

people.name: Vasil Levski
people.why: Organised the independence movement and was hanged by the Ottomans; the national hero.

people.name: Christo
people.why: Wrapped the Reichstag and the Pont Neuf, making landscape-scale art out of fabric.

people.name: John Atanasoff
people.why: Of Bulgarian descent, he built what a US court ruled the first electronic digital computer.

people.name: Grigor Dimitrov
people.why: Bulgaria's most successful tennis player, a former world number three.

people.name: Elisaveta Bagryana
people.why: Brought a modern woman's voice into Bulgarian poetry and was nominated for the Nobel Prize.

events.title: The First Bulgarian Empire
events.what: One of the oldest states in Europe to keep its name unchanged since foundation.

events.title: The Cyrillic alphabet
events.what: Developed at the Preslav school in Bulgaria and now used by some 250 million people.

events.title: Liberation
events.what: The Russo-Turkish war ended five centuries of Ottoman rule; 3 March is the national day.

events.title: Saving the Bulgarian Jews
events.what: Public and parliamentary pressure stopped the deportation of 48,000 Jews to the camps.

culture.label: Roses
culture.text: The Valley of Roses produces much of the world's rose oil, harvested by hand before dawn.

culture.label: Yoghurt
culture.text: Lactobacillus bulgaricus is named after the country, and yoghurt is eaten daily.

culture.label: Gestures
culture.text: A nod means no and a shake means yes — a reliable source of confusion.

culture.label: Martenitsa
culture.text: Red and white threads worn from 1 March until you see a stork, then tied to a tree.

culture.label: Voices
culture.text: Bulgarian women's choral singing was sent into space on the Voyager golden record.

talkAbout: Cyrillic, which Bulgarians will tell you started here.
Martenitsa and spring traditions.
Mountains and hiking — Bulgaria is very mountainous.
avoid: Identity questions with North Macedonia are contentious. The communist period divides generations.

people.name: Milan Rastislav Štefánik
people.why: Co-founded Czechoslovakia and died in a plane crash returning home to it.

people.name: Ľudovít Štúr
people.why: Codified written Slovak, which is why the language exists in its modern form.

people.name: Peter Sagan
people.why: Three consecutive world road race titles, a feat nobody else has managed.

people.name: Zuzana Čaputová
people.why: An environmental lawyer who became Slovakia's first woman president after anti-corruption protests.

people.name: Jozef Murgaš
people.why: A pioneer of wireless telegraphy whose patents fed into early radio.

events.title: Great Moravia
events.what: The first major Slavic state in the region, and where Cyril and Methodius did their work.

events.title: Czechoslovakia founded
events.what: Slovaks and Czechs formed one state out of the collapsing Habsburg empire.

events.title: The Slovak National Uprising
events.what: A large partisan revolt against the German-aligned wartime state, commemorated every August.

events.title: The Velvet Divorce
events.what: Czechoslovakia split into two countries peacefully, by agreement, on New Year's Day.

culture.label: Tatras
culture.text: The High Tatras are the smallest alpine range in the world and the centre of Slovak outdoor life.

culture.label: Castles
culture.text: Around 180 castles and ruins — more per head than almost anywhere.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Bryndzové halušky — potato dumplings with sheep's cheese and bacon — is the national dish.

culture.label: Fujara
culture.text: A three-metre shepherd's flute played over the shoulder, UNESCO-listed.

culture.label: Easter
culture.text: In villages, men still douse women with water and switch them lightly for luck.

talkAbout: The Tatras and hiking.
Castles and folk traditions.
Ice hockey, which is followed intensely.
avoid: Slovakia is not Slovenia, and not a lesser Czech Republic. Roma exclusion is a serious domestic issue.

people.name: Mikalojus Konstantinas Čiurlionis
people.why: Did both at the highest level and anticipated abstraction; died at 35.

people.name: Vytautas the Great
people.why: Ruled Lithuania at its height, when it stretched from the Baltic to the Black Sea.

people.name: Czesław Miłosz
people.why: Nobel laureate born in Lithuania, whose work belongs to the whole region.

people.name: Jonas Mekas
people.why: The godfather of American avant-garde cinema, and a refugee from Lithuania.

people.name: Rūta Meilutytė
people.why: Won Olympic gold at fifteen and set world records in the breaststroke.

events.title: The Grand Duchy
events.what: United with Poland, it was for a time the largest state in Europe.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Lithuania re-established itself after over a century of Russian rule.

events.title: The Baltic Way
events.what: Two million people held hands in a 675 km chain across the three Baltic states.

events.title: First to break away
events.what: Lithuania was the first Soviet republic to declare independence, a year and a half before the USSR fell.

culture.label: Language
culture.text: Lithuanian is among the most archaic living Indo-European languages, and closest to Sanskrit in structure.

culture.label: Hill of Crosses
culture.text: Over 100,000 crosses on a mound near Šiauliai, repeatedly bulldozed by the Soviets and always replaced.

culture.label: Basketball
culture.text: Often called the second religion; Lithuania punches enormously above its weight at it.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Cepelinai potato dumplings, cold beetroot soup that is startlingly pink, and dark rye bread.

culture.label: Amber
culture.text: Baltic amber has been traded from this coast for four thousand years.

talkAbout: Basketball, without fail.
The Baltic Way and 1990.
The language and how old it is.
avoid: Don't call the Baltic states interchangeable, or describe them as ex-Soviet as if that were their identity. Wartime collaboration is a difficult subject.

people.name: Mikhail Baryshnikov
people.why: Born in Riga; among the greatest ballet dancers of the twentieth century.

people.name: Vaira Vīķe-Freiberga
people.why: A refugee who returned to lead Latvia into the EU and NATO.

people.name: Krišjānis Barons
people.why: Collected around 218,000 dainas — the folk songs that carried Latvian identity through occupation.

people.name: Mark Rothko
people.why: Born in Daugavpils; his colour fields are among the most recognisable images in modern art.

people.name: Kristaps Porziņģis
people.why: An NBA champion and Latvia's biggest sporting name.

events.title: Riga founded
events.what: A Hanseatic trading city whose Art Nouveau centre is World Heritage-listed.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Latvia declared independence and then fought for two more years to keep it.

events.title: Occupation
events.what: Soviet, then Nazi, then Soviet again; mass deportations to Siberia in 1941 and 1949.

events.title: The Singing Revolution
events.what: Mass singing demonstrations across the Baltics helped bring down Soviet rule without violence.

culture.label: Song festival
culture.text: Every five years tens of thousands sing together in Riga — UNESCO-listed and central to national identity.

culture.label: Forest
culture.text: More than half the country is forest, and mushroom and berry picking is a national pastime.

culture.label: Jāņi
culture.text: Midsummer, with oak wreaths, cheese, beer and staying up all night.

culture.label: Art Nouveau
culture.text: Riga has the greatest concentration of Art Nouveau architecture of any city in the world.

culture.label: Rye bread
culture.text: Dark sourdough rye is a serious matter, and emigrants have it posted to them.

talkAbout: The song festival and choral singing.
Forests, mushrooms and Jāņi.
Riga's architecture.
avoid: The Soviet occupation and the status of the Russian-speaking minority are both sensitive. Don't merge the three Baltic states.

people.name: Arvo Pärt
people.why: For years the most performed living composer in the world, in his own tintinnabuli style.

people.name: Lennart Meri
people.why: Deported to Siberia as a child, he became the president who anchored Estonia in Europe.

people.name: Jaan Tallinn
people.why: Co-wrote Skype and Kazaa, and now funds work on existential risk.

people.name: Kristjan Raud
people.why: His illustrations of the Kalevipoeg epic shaped Estonia's visual self-image.

people.name: Kelly Sildaru
people.why: Won X Games gold at thirteen, the youngest ever to do so.

events.title: The first song festival
events.what: The beginning of the national awakening, and of the tradition that still defines Estonia.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Declared amid the collapse of the Russian empire and defended in a two-year war.

events.title: Restored independence
events.what: Estonia broke free during the Soviet collapse after years of singing protest.

events.title: Voting online
events.what: Estonia became the first country in the world to hold legally binding national elections over the internet.

culture.label: e-Estonia
culture.text: Almost all government services run online; digital identity is ordinary infrastructure here.

culture.label: Laulupidu
culture.text: The song festival gathers tens of thousands of singers; it was the engine of the Singing Revolution.

culture.label: Sauna
culture.text: As central as in Finland; the smoke sauna tradition of Võromaa is UNESCO-listed.

culture.label: Forest and bogs
culture.text: Half forest, with boardwalks across the bogs and the right to roam.

culture.label: Manner
culture.text: Quiet and understated. Estonians joke about it themselves.

talkAbout: Digital government, which they will happily explain.
The song festival and 1991.
Sauna, bogs and forest walks.
avoid: Estonians are Finnic, not Slavic, and being called Russian is genuinely irritating. The Soviet period and minority-language politics are sensitive.

people.name: Robert Schuman
people.why: Luxembourg-born, his 1950 declaration launched what became the European Union.

people.name: Edward Steichen
people.why: Curated The Family of Man, the most visited photography exhibition ever, now permanently in Luxembourg.

people.name: Grand Duchess Charlotte
people.why: Led the government in exile during the war and became the symbol of Luxembourg's survival.

people.name: Jean-Claude Juncker
people.why: Prime minister for eighteen years, then President of the European Commission.

people.name: Andy Schleck
people.why: Won the Tour de France in 2010, continuing a long Luxembourgish cycling tradition.

events.title: The castle on the Bock
events.what: Count Siegfried's fortress founded the city; the casemates beneath it are World Heritage-listed.

events.title: The Treaty of London
events.what: Guaranteed Luxembourg's independence and neutrality, and required its great fortress to be dismantled.

events.title: The Battle of the Bulge
events.what: The Ardennes offensive tore through the north; Patton is buried at Hamm.

events.title: A European capital
events.what: The Coal and Steel Community set up here, making Luxembourg one of the EU's three seats.

culture.label: Three languages
culture.text: Luxembourgish at home, French in law, German in the press — often in one conversation.

culture.label: Free transport
culture.text: In 2020 Luxembourg became the first country to make all public transport free.

culture.label: Diversity
culture.text: Nearly half the residents are foreign nationals, and more still commute in daily.

culture.label: Echternach
culture.text: The dancing procession at Echternach has been held for centuries and is UNESCO-listed.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Judd mat Gaardebounen — smoked collar of pork with broad beans — plus a Moselle wine tradition.

talkAbout: Languages, and how they switch between them.
Hiking the Mullerthal and the Ardennes.
How a country this small became a European capital.
avoid: Tax-haven jokes land poorly. Don't assume everyone is a banker or that the country is only its financial sector.

people.name: Antoni Fiter i Rossell
people.why: Wrote the Manual Digest, the compilation of Andorran law and custom still cited today.

people.name: Guillem d'Areny-Plandolit
people.why: Led the New Reform of 1866, which broadened the vote and modernised the co-principality.

people.name: Boris Skossyreff
people.why: Declared himself King Boris I of Andorra in 1934 and was removed after eleven days.

people.name: Albert Salvadó
people.why: Andorra's best-known writer, widely translated in Catalan and Spanish.

people.name: Marc Bernaus
people.why: Long-serving captain of the national team and the country's most capped player of his era.

events.title: The paréages
events.what: An agreement between a French count and a Spanish bishop created the shared sovereignty that still governs Andorra.

events.title: The eleven-day king
events.what: Boris Skossyreff proclaimed himself monarch before Spanish police escorted him out.

events.title: Peace with Germany
events.what: Left out of the Versailles treaty, Andorra formally ended its First World War state of war forty years late.

events.title: The constitution
events.what: Andorra adopted a written constitution and joined the United Nations.

culture.label: Co-princes
culture.text: The heads of state are the President of France and the Bishop of Urgell — a 750-year-old arrangement.

culture.label: Skiing
culture.text: Grandvalira is the largest ski area in the Pyrenees and the backbone of the economy.

culture.label: Catalan
culture.text: The only country where Catalan is the sole official language.

culture.label: Contrapàs
culture.text: Traditional dances performed at village festivals, especially in Sant Julià and Andorra la Vella.

culture.label: Mountains
culture.text: Nothing below 800 m, and the Madriu valley is a World Heritage cultural landscape.

talkAbout: Skiing and mountain walking.
The co-principality, which visitors always find strange.
Catalan language and culture.
avoid: Andorra is not part of Spain or France. Duty-free shopping jokes and tax questions get tiresome.

people.name: Svetlana Alexievich
people.why: Won the Nobel Prize in 2015 for oral histories built from thousands of interviews.

people.name: Marc Chagall
people.why: Born in Vitebsk, and its wooden houses and floating figures never left his work.

people.name: Francysk Skaryna
people.why: Printed the first book in an East Slavic language, decades before Moscow had a press.

people.name: Maria Kalesnikava
people.why: Tore up her passport rather than be deported during the 2020 protests; imprisoned since.

people.name: Yanka Kupala
people.why: The national poet, who made Belarusian a modern literary language.

events.title: The Commonwealth
events.what: Belarusian lands were the heart of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania and its union with Poland.

events.title: Occupation
events.what: Belarus lost around a quarter of its population — proportionally more than any other country in the war.

events.title: Chernobyl fallout
events.what: About 70% of the fallout landed on Belarus, contaminating a fifth of its farmland.

events.title: The protests
events.what: Hundreds of thousands marched against a disputed election; the crackdown drove many into exile.

culture.label: Forest
culture.text: Białowieża, Europe's last primeval lowland forest, with wild bison; and vast marshes in Polesia.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Draniki potato pancakes above all, plus machanka and dark bread.

culture.label: Rushnik
culture.text: Woven ritual towels with red geometric patterns, used at weddings and funerals.

culture.label: Memory
culture.text: Khatyn and other war memorials are central to public life; almost every family lost someone.

culture.label: Language
culture.text: Belarusian and Russian are both official; using Belarusian has become a political statement.

talkAbout: Literature and Alexievich's oral histories.
Forests, bison and the countryside.
Food, especially the many uses of potato.
avoid: Politics is genuinely dangerous for Belarusians to discuss. Many abroad are exiles — don't assume anything about their views or their safety.

people.name: Ivo Andrić
people.why: The Bridge on the Drina, set in Višegrad, won the Nobel Prize in 1961.

people.name: Emir Kusturica
people.why: Twice won the Palme d'Or at Cannes, a feat only a handful of directors have managed.

people.name: Mak Dizdar
people.why: Stone Sleeper drew on medieval Bosnian tombstones to make a distinctly Bosnian poetry.

people.name: Jasmila Žbanić
people.why: Quo Vadis, Aida? brought Srebrenica to a worldwide audience and was nominated for an Oscar.

people.name: Edin Džeko
people.why: Bosnia's record scorer and its most recognisable sportsman.

events.title: Ottoman conquest
events.what: Four centuries of Ottoman rule gave Bosnia its mosques, its bridges and much of its cuisine.

events.title: Sarajevo
events.what: Gavrilo Princip's shots on the Latin Bridge began the First World War.

events.title: The Winter Olympics
events.what: Sarajevo hosted the Games; eight years later the bobsleigh track was a firing position.

events.title: The war
events.what: Around 100,000 killed, Sarajevo besieged for 1,425 days, and genocide at Srebrenica.

culture.label: Coffee
culture.text: Bosanska kafa served in a džezva with rahat lokum, and drunk slowly over a long conversation.

culture.label: Sarajevo
culture.text: A mosque, an Orthodox church, a Catholic cathedral and a synagogue within a few hundred metres.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Ćevapi in somun bread, burek by the metre, and a strong pastry tradition.

culture.label: Sevdalinka
culture.text: Melancholy love songs, the Bosnian equivalent of fado or blues.

culture.label: Mostar
culture.text: The rebuilt Stari Most, whose divers leap 24 m into the Neretva.

talkAbout: Coffee and its ritual.
Food, and where the best ćevapi are.
Music, especially sevdah.
avoid: The war, Srebrenica and the ethnic division of the state are heavy and contested. Let people volunteer their own story.

people.name: Zeno of Citium
people.why: Founded Stoicism in Athens; he came from Kition, modern Larnaca.

people.name: Makarios III
people.why: Led Cyprus to independence and served as its first president.

people.name: Marcos Baghdatis
people.why: Reached the Australian Open final in 2006 and made Cyprus a tennis nation for a season.

people.name: Christoforos Savva
people.why: The father of Cypriot modern art, who opened the island's first contemporary gallery.

people.name: Anna Vissi
people.why: One of the biggest-selling Greek-language artists of all time.

events.title: Copper and the Mycenaeans
events.what: Cyprus gave its name to copper and traded it across the Bronze Age Mediterranean.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Cyprus left British rule with a constitution shared between Greek and Turkish Cypriots.

events.title: The division
events.what: A Greek-backed coup was followed by Turkish invasion; the island has been divided since.

events.title: Joining the EU
events.what: Cyprus joined, though EU law is suspended in the north.

culture.label: Meze
culture.text: A Cypriot meze can run to thirty small dishes and take an entire evening.

culture.label: Halloumi
culture.text: Invented here, grilled rather than melted, and now protected by EU designation.

culture.label: Kafenio
culture.text: The village coffee house, where the same men have sat at the same tables for decades.

culture.label: Climate
culture.text: Around 320 sunny days a year, and Troodos ski slopes an hour from the beach.

culture.label: Layers
culture.text: Greek, Roman, Byzantine, Crusader, Venetian, Ottoman and British remains, all on one island.

talkAbout: Food, especially meze and halloumi.
Archaeology and the painted churches of Troodos.
Village life and the kafenio.
avoid: The division of the island, the buffer zone and relations with Turkey are the central national grievance. Follow their lead.

people.name: Ibrahim Rugova
people.why: Led a decade of non-violent resistance and became independent Kosovo's first president.

people.name: Dua Lipa
people.why: Kosovo-Albanian, a global pop star, and the founder of the Sunny Hill festival in Pristina.

people.name: Majlinda Kelmendi
people.why: Won Kosovo's first Olympic medal — gold — at its first Games in 2016.

people.name: Rita Ora
people.why: Born in Pristina, and one of Britain's most successful chart artists.

people.name: Xherdan Shaqiri
people.why: Kosovo-born, a Champions League winner, and a figure of pride across the diaspora.

events.title: The Battle of Kosovo
events.what: The Ottoman victory on the Field of Blackbirds that became central to Serbian identity.

events.title: The war
events.what: Serbian forces expelled around a million Kosovo Albanians; NATO intervened by air.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Kosovo declared independence; about half of UN members recognise it, and Serbia does not.

events.title: First Olympics
events.what: Kosovo competed under its own flag for the first time, and won gold.

culture.label: Youth
culture.text: The youngest population in Europe, with a median age around thirty.

culture.label: Macchiato
culture.text: Pristina's café culture is relentless, and the local macchiato is a point of pride.

culture.label: Monasteries
culture.text: The medieval Serbian Orthodox monasteries at Deçan and Peja are World Heritage sites.

culture.label: Diaspora
culture.text: Huge communities in Switzerland and Germany; summer brings them home in convoys.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Flija, cooked in layers over embers over several hours, and served to a crowd.

talkAbout: Music, and how many international artists have Kosovar roots.
Café culture in Pristina.
The diaspora and summer homecomings.
avoid: Recognition, relations with Serbia and the status of Serb communities are the defining political questions and are unresolved.

people.name: Prince Franz Joseph II
people.why: The first prince to actually live in Liechtenstein, and the one who oversaw its rise to wealth.

people.name: Hans-Adam II
people.why: Won a referendum granting the monarch unusually strong powers for a modern European state.

people.name: Hanni Wenzel
people.why: Won two golds at the 1980 Olympics, making Liechtenstein the smallest country ever to top a Winter Games event.

people.name: Tina Weirather
people.why: World Cup winner and Olympic medallist, from a family of ski champions.

people.name: Josef Gabriel Rheinberger
people.why: A celebrated organ composer and teacher in Munich; Liechtenstein's most significant musician.
