events.title: The principality created
events.what: Two lordships were combined and raised to a principality of the Holy Roman Empire.

events.title: The army disbanded
events.what: Liechtenstein dissolved its 80-man army; it has had none since.

events.title: Customs union with Switzerland
events.what: Liechtenstein adopted the Swiss franc and an open border, which underpins its economy.

events.title: Women get the vote
events.what: The last country in Europe to grant women the national franchise, by a men-only referendum.

culture.label: Doubly landlocked
culture.text: One of only two countries you must cross two others to reach the sea from.

culture.label: National Day
culture.text: On 15 August the prince invites the entire country to the castle garden for a drink.

culture.label: Industry
culture.text: Highly specialised manufacturing — including being the world's largest producer of false teeth.

culture.label: Skiing
culture.text: Malbun is the only ski resort, and it has produced an improbable number of Olympic medallists.

culture.label: Art
culture.text: The princely collections are among the largest private art holdings in the world.

talkAbout: Skiing and the mountains.
National Day at the castle.
How a country of 40,000 organises itself.
avoid: Tax-haven and 'you could walk across it' jokes are well worn. Liechtenstein is not part of Switzerland or Austria.

people.name: Dun Karm Psaila
people.why: The national poet, who wrote the words of the Maltese anthem.

people.name: Jean Parisot de Valette
people.why: Held Malta through the Great Siege of 1565 and founded the capital that bears his name.

people.name: Daphne Caruana Galizia
people.why: Investigated corruption at the highest levels and was killed by a car bomb.

people.name: Dom Mintoff
people.why: Ended the British military presence and reshaped Malta as a non-aligned state.

people.name: Joseph Calleia
people.why: A Hollywood character actor of the 1930s and 40s, and Malta's first international star.

events.title: The megalithic temples
events.what: Ġgantija and its siblings are older than Stonehenge or the pyramids.

events.title: The Great Siege
events.what: The Knights of St John held off a far larger Ottoman force in one of history's famous sieges.

events.title: The wartime siege
events.what: Among the most heavily bombed places on earth; the whole island was awarded the George Cross.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Malta left British rule, becoming a republic ten years later.

culture.label: Language
culture.text: Maltese is Semitic, descended from Arabic, written in Latin script, and full of Italian and English.

culture.label: Festa
culture.text: Every village holds a summer patron-saint festa with brass bands and enormous fireworks.

culture.label: Luzzu
culture.text: Brightly painted fishing boats with the Eye of Osiris on the prow, a habit going back to the Phoenicians.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Pastizzi, rabbit stew, and ftira bread; a mix of Sicilian, Arab and British influences.

culture.label: Catholicism
culture.text: Deeply Catholic, though divorce was only legalised in 2011.

talkAbout: The temples and how old they are.
Village festas and the rivalry between neighbouring bands.
The language and how it works.
avoid: Caruana Galizia's murder and the corruption it exposed are still live and painful. Don't call Maltese a dialect of Italian.

people.name: Stephen the Great
people.why: Ruled Moldavia for 47 years and fought off Ottoman, Polish and Hungarian armies.

people.name: Maria Bieșu
people.why: One of the Soviet Union's great opera singers, and Moldova's most celebrated musician.

people.name: Eugen Doga
people.why: His waltz from Gypsies Are Found Near Heaven is played at weddings across the former USSR.

people.name: Maia Sandu
people.why: An economist who became Moldova's first woman president on an anti-corruption platform.

people.name: Zdob și Zdub
people.why: Moldova's best-known musical export, mixing folk with rock at three Eurovisions.

events.title: The Principality of Moldavia
events.what: A state that at its height covered much of today's Moldova and eastern Romania.

events.title: Bessarabia annexed
events.what: The Russian Empire took the land between the Prut and the Dniester, setting the modern borders.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Moldova left the Soviet Union as it dissolved.

events.title: The Transnistria war
events.what: A short war left a Russian-backed breakaway region on the Dniester, unresolved to this day.

culture.label: Wine
culture.text: Cricova and Mileștii Mici have hundreds of kilometres of cellars; the latter holds the largest collection in the world.

culture.label: Music
culture.text: Fiddle, cimbalom and pan flute, with a wedding tradition that runs for days.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Plăcinte pastries, mămăligă, and sarmale wrapped in vine leaves.

culture.label: Countryside
culture.text: One of the most agricultural countries in Europe, with black soil among the richest anywhere.

culture.label: Cave monasteries
culture.text: Orheiul Vechi has monks' cells carved into a limestone cliff above the Răut.

talkAbout: Wine, and the underground cellars.
Food and family celebrations.
Music, especially at weddings.
avoid: Transnistria, relations with Russia and Romania, and whether the language is Moldovan or Romanian are all contested.

people.name: Grace Kelly
people.why: An Oscar winner who became Princess of Monaco and remains its most famous figure.

people.name: Rainier III
people.why: Ruled for 56 years and turned Monaco from a fading casino town into a financial centre.

people.name: Charles Leclerc
people.why: A Monegasque Formula One driver for Ferrari who won his home Grand Prix in 2024.

people.name: Albert I
people.why: A serious marine scientist who founded the Oceanographic Museum.

people.name: Louis Notari
people.why: Wrote the first literary work in Monégasque and helped save the language.

events.title: The Grimaldis take the rock
events.what: François Grimaldi entered the fortress disguised as a monk — hence the monks on the coat of arms.

events.title: The casino opens
events.what: Monte Carlo's casino rescued the principality's finances and created its image.

events.title: The first Grand Prix
events.what: The street race through the town became the most famous circuit in motorsport.

events.title: Joining the UN
events.what: Monaco became a full member of the United Nations.

culture.label: Grand Prix
culture.text: Barriers go up in the streets each May and the whole country becomes a racetrack.

culture.label: Monégasque
culture.text: A Ligurian dialect, now taught in schools to keep it alive; French is the official language.

culture.label: Oceanography
culture.text: The Oceanographic Museum, founded by a prince, was directed for years by Jacques Cousteau.

culture.label: Density
culture.text: The most densely populated country in the world, on two square kilometres.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Barbagiuan and socca — the cooking is Ligurian and Niçois rather than French.

talkAbout: The Grand Prix and how the circuit is built.
The Oceanographic Museum.
Monégasque, and efforts to keep it spoken.
avoid: Tax-exile jokes get tiresome. Only about a quarter of residents are actually Monegasque citizens, which complicates assumptions.

people.name: Petar II Petrović-Njegoš
people.why: The Mountain Wreath is the central work of Montenegrin and Serbian literature.

people.name: Nikola I
people.why: Ruled for 58 years, married his daughters into half of Europe's courts, and made Montenegro a kingdom.

people.name: Milo Đukanović
people.why: Dominated Montenegrin politics for three decades and led it to independence in 2006.

people.name: Marina Abramović
people.why: Of Montenegrin heritage, and the defining figure of performance art.

people.name: Nikola Mirotić
people.why: Born in Podgorica, a EuroLeague MVP and one of the region's finest players.

events.title: The prince-bishopric
events.what: Montenegro was ruled by Orthodox bishops who were also war leaders.

events.title: Recognised independence
events.what: The Congress of Berlin recognised Montenegro as a sovereign state.

events.title: Absorbed into Yugoslavia
events.what: The kingdom was merged into the new South Slav state, a decision still argued about.

events.title: Independence
events.what: A referendum ended the union with Serbia by a margin of just over half a percent above the threshold.

culture.label: Black mountain
culture.text: The name means black mountain; Durmitor and the Tara canyon are among Europe's deepest.

culture.label: Kotor
culture.text: A walled Venetian town at the head of a fjord-like bay, World Heritage-listed.

culture.label: Leisure
culture.text: Montenegrins joke about their own famous laziness, with a set of mock commandments about resting.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Njeguški pršut ham and cheese from the mountains, seafood on the coast.

culture.label: Čojstvo
culture.text: Humanity and bravery — a traditional code about treating even an enemy honourably.

talkAbout: Mountains, the Tara canyon and hiking.
Kotor and the coast.
Food, especially the mountain ham.
avoid: Montenegrin versus Serbian identity, and the status of the Orthodox church, split the country. The 1990s wars are close by.

people.name: Saint Marinus
people.why: A stonemason who by tradition founded the republic on Monte Titano in 301.

people.name: Giuseppe Garibaldi
people.why: Given refuge here in 1849; the republic's protection of him is a founding point of pride.

people.name: Alessandro Bonci
people.why: A rival of Caruso at the Met, and one of San Marino's best-known figures abroad.

people.name: Alessandra Perilli
people.why: Won San Marino's first Olympic medal in 2021, making it the smallest country ever to medal.

people.name: Marino Moretti
people.why: A leading Italian-language poet and novelist closely associated with the republic.

events.title: Foundation
events.what: By tradition, the world's oldest surviving republic began as a refuge from persecution.

events.title: The statutes
events.what: San Marino's written constitution is the oldest still in force anywhere.

events.title: Sheltering refugees
events.what: The neutral republic took in more than 100,000 refugees — four times its own population.

events.title: The first elected communist government
events.what: San Marino elected a communist-led government, the first anywhere to come to power by ballot.

culture.label: Two captains
culture.text: Two Captains Regent serve as joint heads of state for six months, twice a year, since the 1200s.

culture.label: Three towers
culture.text: The fortresses on Monte Titano are on the flag and on every hilltop view.

culture.label: Crossbow
culture.text: The Palio delle Balestre is shot with medieval crossbows in the main square each September.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Torta tre monti, a layered wafer cake named for the three peaks.

culture.label: Italian, not Italy
culture.text: Culturally Romagnol and Italian-speaking, but a separate state for seventeen centuries.

talkAbout: The two Captains Regent and how the system works.
Being the oldest republic in the world.
The crossbow palio and medieval festival.
avoid: Don't call it part of Italy. Jokes about how small it is or how the football team never wins wear thin.

people.name: Michelangelo
people.why: Painted the Sistine Chapel ceiling and designed St Peter's dome.

people.name: Pope John Paul II
people.why: Travelled more than any pope in history and helped bring down communism in Europe.

people.name: Gian Lorenzo Bernini
people.why: Designed St Peter's Square and much of the Baroque Rome around it.

people.name: Pope Francis
people.why: The first pope from the Americas, who lived in a guesthouse rather than the papal apartments.

people.name: Raphael
people.why: The Raphael Rooms in the Apostolic Palace are among the high points of the Renaissance.

events.title: The first St Peter's
events.what: Constantine built a basilica over what was believed to be the apostle's grave.

events.title: The Papal States
events.what: The popes ruled much of central Italy as temporal monarchs for over a millennium.

events.title: The Lateran Treaty
events.what: Created Vatican City as a sovereign state, ending sixty years of dispute with Italy.

events.title: The Second Vatican Council
events.what: Reformed Catholic worship and its relations with other faiths, including a repudiation of antisemitism.

culture.label: Scale
culture.text: 0.49 km² and around 800 residents — the smallest country in the world by both measures.

culture.label: Museums
culture.text: The Vatican Museums hold one of the greatest art collections anywhere, and the Sistine Chapel.

culture.label: Swiss Guard
culture.text: Recruited from Switzerland since 1506, in a uniform often wrongly credited to Michelangelo.

culture.label: Archives
culture.text: The Vatican Apostolic Archive holds 85 km of shelving going back twelve centuries.

culture.label: Latin
culture.text: The official language of the Holy See; Italian is what is actually spoken day to day.
